policy: Judge likely hostility as an endpoint security engineer. A UPX-marked file rejected by standard UPX is hostile, including when checksum repair later recovers it. Missing tools, I/O errors, timeouts and local size ceilings are analysis limitations.
limits: No samples were executed as applications and no remote malware stages were fetched. Only a reviewed byte-reconstruction routine was emulated with a bounded instruction range and no OS imports.
The large Upgini and agent-commander packages received focused source review, not complete audits.
The third native loader final payload remains unrecovered. A related LookFor specimen was context only; its recovered behavior is not attributed to this sample.

Several source findings are suppressed solely by /qa/ in the original staging path. Final endpoint findings use byte-identical copies under /tmp/hostile-review-inputs; original-path counts are retained for comparison.
The available ML model is feature version 18 while the engine expects 21. Pool decisions use reviewed behavior and explicit policy, not the ML probability.
changes: Restore Python helper-fetched source execution matching for the three audio wheels.
Add bounded literal-program decoding for dictionary JavaScript and offset-array PowerShell; expose typed encoding evidence before decoded-layer rule evaluation.
Detect referrer-gated response evaluation and concealed quiet MSI execution using decoded behavior rather than fixed encoding keys.
Detect secret-RPC-error-derived visitor identity without claiming secret-value theft.
Keep self-mutation/submission under obfuscation rather than infection.
Mark file-specific standard-UPX refusals hostile before attempting checksum repair.
Detect far-negative native window coordinates bound to the CreateWindowEx import and combine with concealed executable-buffer activation.

samples.review_scope: Decoded complete embedded PowerShell; reviewed Python activation
samples.reason: Offset integer array reconstructs a decimal-IP HTTP MSI download followed by quiet, hidden msiexec launch and conditional carrier deletion. Remote MSI was not retrieved.

samples.review_scope: Standard UPX attempt, repaired-body recovery and source/disassembly review; not complete RE
samples.reason: Standard UPX fails with a checksum error. Hostile under the explicit user policy even though repair recovers an analysis copy. Recovered behavior mutates and submits self-copies; this is not evidence of infecting other executables.
